name: Velzatinib
summary: Velzatinib (IDRX-42, GSK6042981) is an oral, selective KIT inhibitor for gastrointestinal stromal tumours, acquired with IDRx in February 2025 ($1.0bn upfront plus a $150mm approval milestone). Two Phase 3s: StrateGIST 3 (NCT07218926, about 450 patients, velzatinib 300 mg daily vs sunitinib after imatinib, PFS primary, readout around mid-2028) comes first, and StrateGIST Frontline (NCT07585266, 800 patients, vs imatinib first line, primary completion 2032-08) later. The model is the second-line launch, in KIT-mutant disease, since StrateGIST 3 excludes KIT/PDGFRA wild-type and PDGFRA exon 18 GIST. Price anchor: Qinlock (ripretinib), the most recent KIT inhibitor approved in GIST, at a January 2026 WAC of $46,620 per 30-day bottle, $567,210 a year. Uptake anchor: sunitinib, the standard second-line drug, reached 275 of 521 (52.8%) patients failing standard-dose imatinib in a Taiwanese nationwide cohort (Hsu et al., Oncotarget 2017).

therapy_mode.source: StrateGIST 3 design (ASCO 2026 TPS11588, doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.16_suppl.TPS11588): velzatinib 300 mg once daily, continuous dosing, PFS primary endpoint
therapy_mode.note: Oral oncology drug taken until progression, so chronic under the house definition
therapy_mode.check: StrateGIST 3 TPS (ASCO 2026, JCO 44:16_suppl TPS11588) as reported by OncLive/Targeted Oncology: velzatinib 300 mg once daily, continuous dosing, vs sunitinib 50 mg 4 weeks on/2 off, PFS primary endpoint. Oral, treated to progression, so chronic under the house definition.

list_price_per_patient.source: Deciphera, Information for Colorado Prescribers of Prescription Drugs, v.3 effective 2026-01-01 (https://www.deciphera.com/sites/default/files/2026-01/CO%20Disclosure%20Form%20Final%20v.3%202026.01.01.Q.pdf): Qinlock 50 mg, 90-count bottle, WAC $46,620. Label dose is 150 mg (three tablets) once daily (Qinlock USPI), so one bottle is 30 days: 46,620 x 365/30 = $567,210 a year
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement: this is a published list price, which the brief puts ahead of the CMS convention, but it belongs to the comparator and not to velzatinib. Qinlock is the closest marketed KIT inhibitor in GIST. The book's drug_demand table has no Qinlock, Ayvakit, Gleevec or Sutent rows, and data.cms.gov was unreachable, so no CMS per-beneficiary price could be read. The case against: Qinlock is a fourth-line drug for a very small population, and a second-line drug, or later a first-line one, may launch below it. The generic comparators (sunitinib, imatinib) cost a small fraction of this. Stivarga, the only GIST-labelled drug in drug_demand, is $55,963 per Part D beneficiary (2024), but most of its use is in colorectal cancer, where treatment is short, so it does not show an annual GIST price
list_price_per_patient.check: Deciphera Colorado prescriber disclosure v.3, effective 2026-01-01 (URL as given): Qinlock 50 mg tablet, 90-count bottle, WAC $46,620.00, confirmed by search. Qinlock USPI dose is 150 mg (three 50 mg tablets) once daily, so a bottle is 30 days; the PI was surfaced by search but its dose text was not re-read here. Arithmetic: 46,620 x 365/30 = $567,210 = 0.56721 mm USD per patient-year, unit right. Book check: drug_demand has no Qinlock, Ayvakit, Sutent or Gleevec rows (Sutent and Gleevec exist as assets 1354 and 1196 with no demand), and Stivarga is $55,963 per Part D beneficiary in 2024, as stated. Labelled judgement (fourth-line comparator's price for a second-line entrant) with its case against given; a published list price is allowed by the brief over the CMS convention.

gross_to_net_pct.source: The discount the book already uses on WAC-based prices, reused by name (as the dazukibart and VX-147 seeds use it): Kalydeco's CMS Part D 2024 spend per beneficiary of $273,600 is 72.2% of its $378,786 WAC (vrtx_prices.csv)
gross_to_net_pct.note: Judgement. The house 0.5 is calibrated to a CMS per-beneficiary price, not to a WAC, so it does not apply here. Direction checked: 27.8% comes off list, so net is $409,700 per patient-year. The case against: this is a cystic fibrosis drug's ratio, not an oncology one. Oral oncology is a protected Part D class with thin rebates, which argues for a smaller discount. 340B and Medicaid statutory rebates argue for a larger one. No GIST-specific measure was found
gross_to_net_pct.check: Book check: Kalydeco CMS Part D 2024 is $28,727,989 over 105 beneficiaries = $273,600 (lookup.py demand); its WAC in the book is $29,057.52 per 28 days x 365/28 = $378,786; 273,600/378,786 = 0.7223, so 0.2777 off. The same 0.2777 is carried on the WAC-anchored Dazukibart seed (Lisraya WAC) and on VX-147, as the researcher says. Direction right: 567,210 x 0.7223 = $409,696 net. Updated brief says a WAC anchor takes neither house convention and needs a sourced discount; this is the book's existing sourced analogue, labelled a judgement with its case against. Caveat to carry: the book's own Kalydeco row calls 0.2777 a FLOOR, and backend/gross_to_net.py explains CMS per-beneficiary spend is gross of rebates and below a full year because of partial fills, so the ratio mostly measures fill coverage, not rebates; the true discount is likely larger.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: StrateGIST 1 Phase 1b, second-line cohort, ASCO 2026: median PFS 13.7 months (95% CI 8.6-18.4) at 18.4 months' follow-up (OncLive, 'Velzatinib Shows Activity Across Treatment Lines and KIT Mutation Profiles in Advanced GIST'; Targeted Oncology, same meeting)
discontinuation_pct.note: Constant hazard from a median: 1 - 0.5^(12/13.7) = 0.455, the form the vepugratinib and ABBV-1480 seeds use. The brief's 1 - exp(-12/13.7) gives 0.584 because it treats the median as a mean. The case against: this is a single-arm cohort of about 49 patients with a wide CI. Sunitinib, the Phase 3 comparator, had a median PFS of 8.3 months in INTRIGUE's second-line population, which gives 0.63. If velzatinib wins the trial, its PFS should sit between the two
discontinuation_pct.check: StrateGIST 1 second-line cohort, ASCO 2026 (JCO 44:16_suppl 11520; OncLive and Targeted Oncology reports): median PFS 13.7 months (95% CI 8.6-18.4) at a median follow-up of 18.4 months, confirmed by search. 1 - 0.5^(12/13.7) = 0.4551. Same form the book's vepugratinib seed uses (12.5 months -> 0.4859, which reproduces). Unit right. Cohort size (about 49) not independently checked; it is only in the note.

forecast_start_year.source: StrateGIST 3 (NCT07218926), estimated primary completion 2028-05-30, recruiting since December 2025 (GSK study register trial 300383, https://www.gsk-studyregister.com/trials/300383; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07218926)
forecast_start_year.note: Judgement on timing, using the book's pipeline convention: first full year two calendar years after the earliest Phase 3 primary completion. Readout in mid-2028, filing late 2028, launch around 2029. The date came through a search summary of the GSK register, which could not be opened directly, so the second reader should confirm it. The first-line trial in the context file (NCT07585266, primary completion 2032-08-30) would give 2034 if it were the launch trial instead
forecast_start_year.check: StrateGIST 3 (NCT07218926) is a GSK-funded Phase 3, 450 patients, recruiting since December 2025 (OncLive, Targeted Oncology, Duke, MSKCC listings). The exact 2028-05-30 primary completion date could not be seen (Amass at its usage limit, ClinicalTrials.gov blocked, two searches returned no date), but the GSK register (trial 300383) gives a primary-endpoint timeframe of up to about 130 weeks, which from a December 2025 start lands around June 2028, consistent with it. Book convention of two calendar years after primary completion (vepugratinib seed: 2029-10 -> 2031) gives 2030. Labelled judgement.

exus_multiple.source: GSK FY2025 annual report Specialty Medicines turnover table (0001654954-26-000892, via the book's asset_revenue_regions): Ojjaara/Omjjara GBP 417mm US, 98mm Europe, 39mm International; (98+39)/417 = 0.3285
exus_multiple.note: Judgement on the comparator. Ojjaara is GSK's most recent oral targeted oncology launch. Jemperli gives almost the same figure (214/647 = 0.331). Zejula (0.91) reflects an older European base. The case for higher: GIST is treated in Europe and Asia with KIT inhibitors, and Novartis's Gleevec and Tasigna sold more outside the US (Tasigna 618/486 in FY2025). The case for lower: ex-US payers may not fund a premium over generic sunitinib
exus_multiple.check: Book asset_revenue_regions FY2025, source 'annual report table 0001654954-26-000892': Ojjaara US GBP 417mm, Europe 98mm, International 39mm; (98+39)/417 = 0.3285. Jemperli 159+55 over 647 = 0.3308; Zejula (215+50)/292 = 0.91; Tasigna 618/486 USD. All as stated. Labelled judgement on the comparator with cases both ways.

economics_share.source: GSK completes acquisition of IDRx, Inc. (GSK press release, February 2025, https://www.gsk.com/en-gb/media/press-releases/gsk-completes-acquisition-of-idrx-inc/): 100% acquired, up to $1.15bn
economics_share.note: GSK owns the asset outright. It still owes success-based milestones and tiered royalties on IDRX-42 to Merck KGaA, Darmstadt (per the same release). The rates are not disclosed and this field does not capture them, so net economics are somewhat below 1.0. The $150mm approval milestone to IDRx holders is also not modelled here
economics_share.check: GSK press releases 'GSK enters agreement to acquire IDRx' (January 2025) and 'GSK completes acquisition of IDRx' (search confirmed): all equity acquired for up to $1.15bn, $1bn upfront plus a $150mm regulatory approval milestone; GSK is responsible for success-based milestones and tiered royalties on IDRX-42 owed to Merck KGaA, Darmstadt. 1.0 is right for ownership; the note correctly flags the undisclosed royalty.

prevalence.source: Set equal to incidence by the book's line-of-therapy convention (forecast.py: a pool stated equal to its own inflow is each year's patients, with carryover 0)
prevalence.note: lookup.py pool returns nothing for GIST, so the book carries no figure and this seed supplies one. This is the second-line line of therapy, not the living GIST population
prevalence.check: lookup.py pool 'Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors' returns nothing (the book carries only 'Gastrointestinal Neoplasms', a different name), so the seed must supply it. backend/forecast.py lines 171-172: when prevalence equals incidence and no carryover is stated, carryover and the stock are set to 0, so each year's flow is the pool, as the source says.

incidence.source: Patel N, Benipal B. Incidence of GIST in the United States 2001-2015: a USCS analysis of 50 states. Cureus 2019;11(2):e4120, doi:10.7759/cureus.4120 (PMID 31037234): overall incidence 0.70 per 100,000 a year, applied to the 340,110,988 US residents of July 2024 (Census Vintage 2024)
incidence.note: The rate is age-adjusted to the 2000 standard and averaged over 2001-2015. It rose about 5% a year over that period (APC 4.44 in males, 5.40 in females), so the current rate is likely higher. The same paper counts 34,257 cases over 15 years, 2,284 a year
incidence.check: Patel & Benipal, Cureus 2019;11(2):e4120 (PMID 31037234, full text read): overall GIST incidence 0.70 per 100,000 a year 2001-2015, age-adjusted to the 2000 US standard; 34,257 cases; APC 4.44 (males) and 5.40 (females). 0.70 x 340,110,988 / 100,000 = 2,380.8 -> 2,381. Census Vintage 2024 July 2024 population of 340,110,988 matches the Census release. Note on the rising, age-adjusted rate is fair.

eligible_pct.source: Three sourced parts. (1) 5,234 of 31,019 staged cases (16.87%) were distant at diagnosis (Patel & Benipal, Cureus 2019;11(2):e4120, PMID 31037234, Table 1). (2) Estimated 15-year recurrence-free survival after surgery without adjuvant therapy was 59.9%, so 40.1% recur (Joensuu H et al., Lancet Oncol 2012;13:265-74, doi:10.1016/S1470-2045(11)70299-6, PMID 22153892, 2,560 patients pooled). 0.1687 + 0.8313 x 0.401 = 0.5021 of each year's diagnoses reach advanced disease. (3) The label reach: StrateGIST 3 (NCT07218926; ASCO 2026 TPS11588) excludes GIST that is wild-type for both KIT and PDGFRA and GIST with an activating PDGFRA exon 18 mutation. In advanced GIST (MetaGIST) KIT mutations are found in 82.8% and PDGFRA in 2.1% (Emile JF et al., Med Oncol 2012;29(3):1765-72, doi:10.1007/s12032-011-0074-y, PMID 21953054). 0.5021 x 0.828 = 0.4157
eligible_pct.note: Judgement: assumes every KIT-mutant patient reaching advanced disease eventually fails imatinib and is fit for a second line, and that the label follows the trial's exclusions. The case for lower: adjuvant imatinib now delays or prevents some recurrences, some patients stay on first-line imatinib for years, and some die or decline before second line. The case for higher: the incidence rate is out of date and rising, and non-exon-18 PDGFRA mutants (a share of the 2.1%) are eligible but left out here
eligible_pct.check: Arithmetic of the researcher's two parts holds (paper table: 5,234/31,019 distant; Joensuu abstract: 15-year RFS 59.9% in 2,560 unadjuvanted patients), giving 0.502. But the pool was not the label's: StrateGIST 3 excludes KIT/PDGFRA wild-type and PDGFRA exon 18 GIST (TPS11588 as reported by OncLive), and the researcher's note left the KIT share unsourced. Applied the 82.8% KIT-mutant share in advanced GIST from Emile et al. 2012 (abstract read via PubMed): 0.5016 -> 0.4157 (0.5021 x 0.828, using the exact 5,234/31,019).

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of each year's eligible patients
penetration_peak_pct.source: Hsu JT et al., 'Imatinib dose escalation versus sunitinib as a second-line treatment against advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors: a nationwide population-based cohort study', Oncotarget 2017;8(41):71128-37, doi:10.18632/oncotarget.16795, PMID 29050348 (Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database, July 2004 to December 2010): of 521 advanced GIST patients failing first-line imatinib 400 mg and treated with dose escalation or sunitinib, 125 escalated then switched to sunitinib and 150 switched directly, so 275 (52.8%) received sunitinib after imatinib; 150 (28.8%) took it directly
penetration_peak_pct.note: Judgement: the multiple is 1.0 on sunitinib's post-imatinib capture, assuming a head-to-head PFS win in StrateGIST 3 takes sunitinib's place. The anchor is sunitinib at any point after imatinib, including after dose escalation, because velzatinib's trial population is 'after imatinib' and escalation is still imatinib. The case for lower: the denominator excludes patients who received neither option (best supportive care, death before second line), so it overstates capture of the model's pool; the setting is Taiwan, not the US. The case for higher: sunitinib was reimbursed in Taiwan only from February 2009, part way through the 2004-2010 enrolment window, so its share there is depressed; a PFS win could also displace dose escalation
penetration_peak_pct.check: The researcher's source (Huang S et al., Transl Oncol 2023;30:101641, PMID 36791510, PMC9950928, abstract read) does not say what the field claims: it examined 240 patients selected for having received sunitinib for at least 8 weeks, at three Chinese tertiary centres, 2008-2016. The 103 of 203 (50.7%) is the share of eventual sunitinib users who switched directly rather than escalating first; all 203 received sunitinib, so it is not sunitinib's capture of patients failing imatinib. Replaced with a population-based cohort whose denominator is all imatinib failures treated with either option (full text read via PubMed): 275/521 = 0.5278. 0.507 -> 0.5278.

ramp_steepness.source: book: Enhertu's CMS Part B launch fit (864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105, 8,410 beneficiaries 2020-2024), k=1.08, midpoint 2.2 years, carried by the ABBV-1480, ABBV-706, camizestrant and vepugratinib seeds
ramp_steepness.note: Reuses a measured oncology curve. The book has no GIST launch to fit
ramp_steepness.check: lookup.py demand Enhertu: Part B beneficiaries 864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105, 8,410 over 2020-2024, as stated. k = 1.08 with midpoint 2.2 carried in the book by ABBV-1480, ABBV-706, camizestrant, vepugratinib and others. Reuse of a measured oncology curve; the book has no GIST launch.

ramp_midpoint_year.source: as ramp_steepness (Enhertu fit carried in the book)
ramp_midpoint_year.check: Same Enhertu fit as ramp_steepness: midpoint 2.2 years, carried by the ABBV-1480, camizestrant and vepugratinib seeds (book assumptions checked).
